source.title: Deep Linear Network Training Dynamics from Random Initialization: Data, Width, Depth, and Hyperparameter Transfer

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops training-dynamics theory for deep linear networks and reports power-law loss decay over training iterations, but does not test the listed language-model scaling-law versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses neural scaling laws in its background and reports its own loss-versus-training-time power laws. It does not measure held-out language-model loss against parameters, tokens, or compute, nor test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The power-law results below are recorded as related findings, not as tests of a listed version. Cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is a DMFT theory of deep linear networks (synthetic Gaussian/power-law data). Its power laws are in training iterations only; it does not measure language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute, nor allocation, shape at fixed parameters, downstream tasks or fit choices. Width/depth effects are shown as 'wider is better' and convergence-to-limit curves, not power-law fits on language models. Its results therefore bear on no listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude their DMFT captures how width, depth, data, batch size and richness affect deep linear network dynamics, including 'wider is better' and hyperparameter transfer in µP/depth-µP (failing in NTK). It also recovers accelerated power-law training-time exponents for hard tasks that are the same across depths. They note edge-of-stability effects may alter this at long times, and that the model is limited to linear networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports dynamics that vary with parameterization, width, depth, dataset or batch size, richness, and task regime; these are not tests of the listed scaling-law versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In deep linear networks (L=4, also L=1 case) on power-law covariates in the rich regime, infinite-width test loss decays as t^(-2β/(1+β)) for hard tasks (β<1) and t^(-β) for easy tasks (β≥1). The exponent is independent of depth, and finite width eventually slows convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In linear-network models of scaling, feature learning accelerates the loss-vs-time exponent for hard tasks, and this exponent is the same across depths.

fits_no_version.finding: In µP, loss improves monotonically with width and the optimal learning rate transfers across widths. In NTK parameterization the optimal learning rate shifts with width. With 1/√L branch scaling, the learning rate also transfers across depth (Figs 1, 2, 5, 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hyperparameter transfer across width and depth depends on parameterization (µP and depth-µP vs NTK and unscaled ResNets).

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: The model class is limited to deep linear networks. The reported power-law result concerns loss versus training iterations on structured data, not language-model loss versus model size, tokens, or compute. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported asymptotic laws.

untested.parts: All: no LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no extrapolation from small to large runs.
All: depth and width effects shown in linear toy networks, not at fixed parameter count for LMs.
All: synthetic linear regression is not a tested modality or regime of the claim's laws in N/D/C.
All: no fitted scaling-law exponents compared across setups.

record.verdict_notes: Hoffmann et al. is cited only as background, via prior linear random-feature models that recover Chinchilla-like laws; that is not this paper's own result. The rows are correctly unlinked, and no verdict labels are warranted.
